facts.detail: Checker covers indoor/outdoor calls, 3G and 4G, plus outdoor 5G.
Access uses a postcode or permitted location detection.
Results provide a local summary and interactive map.
Operator data is converted into computer-model signal predictions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Predictions are not observed parcel signal measurements.

facts.detail: Reports indoor/outdoor 4G and 5G as good or variable.
Performance dials estimate video-streaming likelihood across a postal district.
Trees, buildings and walls can make experience differ from predictions.
In-home results are averaged and explicitly guide-only.

guard_streams.write_limit: District averages cannot become exact address measurements.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Map Your Mobile checker update

facts.detail: Updated coverage uses 50-metre squares where data permits, versus 100 metres previously.
Indoor and outdoor predictions are separated.
Variable outdoor coverage usually supports voice, text and lower-quality video.
Good outdoor coverage gives higher confidence for streaming.

guard_streams.write_limit: Granularity and qualitative classes remain predictions.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom tackling consumer confusion about broadband technology

facts.detail: Fibre alone can ambiguously describe FTTC, FTTP or cable.
27% of customers lacked confidence in provider terminology.
Only 46% claiming full fibre lived where it was available.
Clear terms include cable, copper, full-fibre and part-fibre.

guard_streams.write_limit: Terminology research does not prove parcel technology.

facts.detail: Providers should not use fibre alone.
Full-fibre means fibre from exchange to home.
Part-fibre usually means fibre to cabinet then copper.
Technology must be disclosed at sale, before purchase and in contract documents.

guard_streams.write_limit: Sales disclosure is not independent parcel verification.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom checklist for a new phone or broadband contract

facts.detail: Summary is one page, or up to three for bundles.
It includes charges, term and cancellation process.
Detailed written information is due before the customer is bound.
Ofcom points users to accredited comparison services.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract documents do not establish parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Contract terms must be fair and transparent.
Protections include residential and small-business customers up to ten employees.
Non-beneficial changes require at least one month's notice.
Affected customers receive a penalty-free exit right.

guard_streams.write_limit: Account rights cannot populate parcel fields.

guard_streams.source: January 2026 OMR and premises in BDUK plans

facts.detail: Release published 4 June 2026.
Edition applies to England and Wales.
Covers OMR status, connectivity, commercial plans and BDUK interventions.
Provides regional ZIPs and a sample CSV for technical use.

guard_streams.write_limit: BDUK planning data cannot replace accepted Ofcom r2 evidence.

guard_streams.source: January 2026 UPRN release user guide and technical note

facts.detail: Uses Dec-2025 NSUL and Nov-2025 NSPL/ONSUD vintages.
BDUK recommends programming software; spreadsheets may omit rows.
Updates are planned with OMR closures about every four months.
AddressBase-derived base excludes demolished and non-postal records.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reference vintages cannot be silently reconciled with Ofcom data.

guard_streams.source: January 2026 UPRN release user guide and technical note

facts.detail: White means no current or likely three-year gigabit infrastructure.
Grey/Black means one or more current or planned qualifying infrastructures.
Under Review marks unverified claims or delivery/evidence risk.
GIS scope separates initial, deferred and in-procurement premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Planning classifications do not prove live orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK gigabit subsidy wholesale access and pricing guidance

facts.detail: Pricing guidance applies to approved GIS projects.
It sets obligations for successful subsidised bidders.
Projects require wholesale price benchmarking and control.
OMR and Public Review submissions alone carry no open-access duty.

guard_streams.write_limit: Wholesale controls do not establish retail parcel service.

guard_streams.source: BDUK wholesale open access network requirements

facts.detail: Requirements cover direct and indirect subsidy recipients.
They support UK Subsidy Control compliance.
They are legally separate from communications regulation.
They must be read with wholesale pricing rules.

guard_streams.write_limit: Wholesale-access duties do not prove address coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK OMR and Public Review subsidy classification guidance

facts.detail: OMR/PR identifies areas potentially needing subsidy.
Targets premises lacking current or likely three-year gigabit infrastructure.
Market intelligence is used to avoid subsidised overbuild.
Guidance estimated roughly 20% might not be reached commercially.

guard_streams.write_limit: Subsidy classification does not establish parcel state.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Openreach framework and July 2026 management release

facts.detail: Framework records eight awarded call-offs.
Call-off three is £150.5m for 65,120 contracted premises.
July release snapshots data held 16 July 2026.
Figures are initial-scope, rounded, lagged and not directly comparable with official statistics.

guard_streams.write_limit: Framework and management totals cannot identify parcel delivery.

guard_streams.source: Canonical slot state and exact-output acceptance

facts.detail: No live owner exists.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING exists.
Terminal continuation/runtime records remain the ownership fallback.
No promotion is allowed before accepted r2 bytes and exact postjoin evidence.

guard_streams.write_limit: Final completion still requires canonical Windows-host validation.
